stem: A triangular field in Sindh, Pakistan, is divided by a straight fence \(\overline{DE}\) that is parallel to side \(\overline{BC}\), as shown. The fence cuts off triangle \(ADE\), whose area is one fourth of the area of the whole field \(ABC\). The fence is 50 meters long. What is the length, in meters, of side \(\overline{BC}\)?
solution: Because \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\). If the scale factor from \(ADE\) to \(ABC\) is \(k\), the areas are in the ratio \(1 : k^{2}\).

explanation.A: Correct. The area ratio \(1 : 4\) means the length ratio is \(1 : 2\), so \(BC = 100\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This multiplies 50 by 4, the area ratio; lengths scale by the square root of the area ratio, which is 2.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This divides 50 by 2; \(\overline{BC}\) belongs to the larger triangle, so it must be longer than the fence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This multiplies 50 by 3 because the rest of the field has 3 times the area of \(ADE\); the length ratio comes from comparing \(ADE\) with the whole triangle \(ABC\).

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['D'][1]==P['E'][1] and P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]
ar=lambda *o: Rational(1,2)*abs(sum(P[o[i]][0]*P[o[(i+1)%len(o)]][1]-P[o[(i+1)%len(o)]][0]*P[o[i]][1] for i in range(len(o))))
assert ar('A','D','E')/ar('A','B','C')==Rational(1,4)
k=sqrt(Rational(4,1))
ans=50*k
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==100
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
